standard.title: NDDev CI/CD Workflows
standard.purpose: Define a public modular CI/CD contract and reusable implementation with complete applicable feedback, no additional spend and coherent artifact delivery.
applies-to: The selected CI/CD library modules and their authorized project invocations, including source validation, build artifacts, delivery and maintenance.
excludes: GitHub task tracking, branches, merge policy and agent task execution owned by the applicable STD-0002/STD-0003 editions.
Repository structure and common standards authoring owned by STD-0001 and STD-0000.
Purchases, paid overage, visibility changes to existing private repositories and automatic fleet-wide adoption.
A new runner manager, agent scheduler, universal source analyzer, prose-attestation platform or credentials database.
Claiming universal language, hardware, security or production correctness from a schema or a finite test suite.
standard.conformance: A selected implementation or invocation conforms when its actual behavior meets every applicable active requirement. The standard uses explicit review criteria; the implementation binds genuine automated checks only to properties they establish. Unavailable or unexecuted work is not passed. Technical modules are independently usable; private authoring tools are not runtime dependencies. NDDev departures follow actual scoped user decisions.

relations.note: NDDev engineering execution; no proprietary corpus is imported into public runtime.
NDDev GitHub workflow; CI/CD consumes the established integration model.

verification.establishes: Real Rust/C++ fuzz runs, retained crash inputs, caught/missed native mutation outcomes and paired benchmark measurements exercise positive and deliberate failure cases. No application-wide quality or speed claim follows.
The real Import Linter fixture accepts the correct graph and rejects a forbidden reverse dependency/cycle and an unmatched scope through tests/run_native.py.
Selected artifact bytes, executable modes and content/source identities survive packaging/unpacking; traversal, tampering and unrelated source are rejected.
Owned native lock/reclamation scenarios preserve foreign and active data; native Rust fixtures measure target/sccache reuse with bounded stores. Host capacity remains an owner observation.

Native process/Git regressions cover requirements-only command selection, explicit non-applicability, manager lock resolution, named manifests, bounded diagnostics, YAML merge handling, isolated outputs and owned cleanup. Main scope cases retain affected native platform cells and advanced dependents. Mocked API cases cover feedback marker/attempt and pagination contracts; they do not establish live publication.

Existing current files/directories are refused before backup, migration, release or pending-state creation and their bytes remain intact. The core static delivery scenario also exercises a successful subsequent activation through the owned current symlink.

Native static HTTP, an isolated Compose project, a temporary systemd service, HTTPS package publication with consumer install, and native-validated Android APK/AAB packages exercise the selected adapters. Invalid-operation regressions additionally prove that backup/migration never starts on known invalid input. This is not production/store acceptance.
Current local links and canonical generation drift are checked. Executable doctests and Flutter localization generation exercise native examples; prose truth remains review.
Declared native external transport/access limits remain unavailable with Issue references; broken responses remain failures. Findings still need project-specific review.
Real submodule gitlinks/worktrees match, and stale/dirty/symlinked or command-modified inputs cannot pass source validation.
Actual native target scenarios expose the tested revision. Compose inspection also checks selected running immutable image identities; generic HTTP success is insufficient.
Actual Git deletion/rename, dependents and missing-base cases retain required scopes. The separate consumer-contract binding covers anchored recursive globs, root locks and successful-main baselines.

Validation cannot silently replace tracked nested ecosystem locks or explicitly selected inputs. Consumer regressions mutate a nested bun lock and reject it; artifact manifests also bind actual source/tree/run/callee identities.

Native run-binding logic rejects mismatched source trees/attempts and obsolete main revisions. Main-baseline regressions preserve changes from unverified pushes. Actual main-run API/download execution supplements these finite cases.

Native Buildx creates a real OCI archive; strict TLS registry publication preserves its digest, a real running image serves the revision, and corruption/build errors fail. Selected Linux x64 does not establish every platform.
Known invalid service, project, registry and payload inputs invoke neither backup nor migration and leave the target unchanged.
Real SIGTERM-resistant descendants are terminated after timeout and cancellation even when their leader exits. Core cases also exercise startup failure, exit status and logs.
Selected native fixtures build/test/package real source and reject deliberate errors. This covers the declared finite SDK/OS cells, not every SDK or hardware target.
A real isolated SQLite backup/migration followed by failed health remains pending without incompatible file rollback; recovery verifies the same resource and does not repeat the migration.
Native wheel/sdist inventory through Syft preserves selected bytes/modes and rejects tampering; the public workflow separately establishes actual GitHub signatures on an eligible candidate.

Actual SSH/SCP reaches a separate server/filesystem; pinned host-key failure, exact artifact receipts, two-client target exclusion and partial migration recovery are exercised. Production targets and arbitrary server toolchains remain unverified.
Native positive collection and missing/empty/all-skipped result rejection. Whole workflow job expectations are additionally checked by its final gate.
Selected native report bytes are retained after failure while escaping paths are rejected. Native upload jobs retain the bounded actual result artifact.
Public Linux/Windows/macOS refuse provider switching. Private admission/trust and malformed-policy cases run in the core suite; actual account entitlements remain review.
Independent real processes racing one target cannot both replace the same previous state. Stale attempts are rejected by the same target-owned state/lock.

sources.title: Android Developers: apkanalyzer
sources.supports: The SDK can parse an actual APK binary manifest into XML.
sources.limits: A parsed manifest does not establish signing, application correctness or store acceptance.

sources.title: Android Developers: bundletool
sources.supports: Native bundle validation and manifest inspection use the Android toolchain.
sources.limits: Toolchain availability must be established; structural validation does not certify signatures or stores.

sources.title: Original fuzz harness source
sources.supports: Original Rust fuzz target and lock under rust/fuzz and C++ harness under fuzzing/checksum_fuzzer.cpp; adjacent native NOTICE files preserve their grants.
sources.limits: The public library does not import the earlier policy or paid capability platform.

sources.title: Original native fixture source
sources.supports: Original Python, Rust, Go, C++, Qt, Flutter, Node, Swift, R, SQL and Android fixtures adapted under tests/native with original grants and notices.
sources.limits: Original presence is not proof of executed native verification; current workflows select actual tests.

sources.title: ArchUnit
sources.supports: JVM architecture tests can express dependency, layer and cycle constraints.
sources.limits: No fixed hexagonal directory skeleton or proof of all design quality follows.

sources.title: Blacksmith: pricing
sources.supports: Free and paid service surfaces and possible OSS arrangements are separate.
sources.limits: No sponsorship or approval for NDDev is established by this page; verify actual account and terms.

sources.title: Blacksmith: instance types and free units
sources.supports: The free pool is 3000 normalized x64 2-vCPU minutes per organization/month, with platform conversions; runner/app coverage matters.
sources.limits: This is a dated observation, not a guarantee of account entitlement, unlimited wall-clock minutes or a hard billing stop.

sources.title: Blacksmith: settings
sources.supports: GitHub login, inherited organization membership and spending notification behavior.
sources.limits: An email alert after exceeding a threshold is not evidence of zero-overage enforcement.

sources.title: Cargo: build cache
sources.supports: Target outputs and intermediate build directories can have different locations; native tooling describes what is reusable.
sources.limits: Supported environment variables depend on Cargo version; build-dir layout alone does not establish cache correctness.

sources.title: Cargo: configuration
sources.supports: Global download-cache cleanup is separate from project build-output retention.
sources.limits: Configuration defaults and availability must match the selected Cargo version.

sources.title: dependency-cruiser
sources.supports: Dependency graph rules can detect forbidden edges and cycles in JS/TS projects.
sources.limits: Project resolution settings and dynamic/framework entrypoints must be considered.

sources.title: Docker: GitHub Actions cache backend
sources.supports: Cache scope and export/import choices affect BuildKit reuse and transfer costs.
sources.limits: A backend is not automatically free; cache mounts and final artifacts have distinct lifecycles.

sources.title: DORA: continuous integration
sources.supports: Fast and reliable integrated feedback supports delivery quality.
sources.limits: Team-level empirical guidance does not prescribe a fixed number of agents, jobs, reruns or approvals.

sources.title: GitHub: upload-artifact
sources.supports: Artifact packaging, permission behavior, compression and retention options.
sources.limits: Action version and actual payload need verification. An artifact digest alone is not authenticated provenance.

sources.title: GitHub: Actions billing
sources.supports: Standard public hosted execution and self-hosted execution have distinct billing from private hosted use and storage.
sources.limits: Actual allowance, budgets and account policy must be observed; no fixed number is a perpetual standard guarantee.

sources.title: GitHub: composite actions
sources.supports: Shared steps execute inside a caller-owned job.
sources.limits: A composite action does not select a job runner or safely hide arbitrary untrusted commands.

sources.title: GitHub: workflow concurrency
sources.supports: Concurrency groups and cancellation are repository-scoped coordination mechanisms.
sources.limits: A deployment-attempt key does not serialize one target; no cross-repository lock is implied.

sources.title: GitHub: workflow events
sources.supports: PR contexts, merge refs and downstream event semantics differ.
sources.limits: An event or successful old run alone does not prove the integrated artifact is eligible.

sources.title: GitHub: reuse workflow configurations
sources.supports: Caller context, permission propagation and self-hosted runner visibility constrain reusable workflow composition.
sources.limits: Provider limits and access rules are version-sensitive. This is not proof of a specific cross-organization installation.

sources.title: GitHub: Actions secrets
sources.supports: Repository-scoped secrets, fork restrictions and private-Free organization-secret limitations.
sources.limits: Access does not authorize a deployment; masking is not complete data-loss prevention.

sources.title: GitHub: secure use of Actions
sources.supports: Privileged event, untrusted code, token and persistent self-hosted runner trust boundaries.
sources.limits: The implementation needs appropriate concrete controls, not a claim that every container is isolated.

sources.title: Import Linter
sources.supports: Python import, layer and independence contracts are directly checkable.
sources.limits: Import graphs do not establish complete semantic architecture or all dynamic dependencies.

sources.title: OSV-Scanner
sources.supports: Native dependency and vulnerability analysis can support non-commercial-service-dependent scanning.
sources.limits: Database freshness, supported lock formats and tool errors need explicit handling.

sources.title: Python: doctest
sources.supports: Executable examples can be checked against actual program output.
sources.limits: Only executed examples are established; adjacent prose is not mechanically certified.

sources.title: sccache: local storage
sources.supports: Local backend ownership and bounded storage must match the server model.
sources.limits: Independent concurrent servers must not be assumed safe on one storage directory.

sources.title: sccache: Rust constraints
sources.supports: Rust cache eligibility and incremental-compilation interactions constrain useful configurations.
sources.limits: The cache does not cover every linked result, and performance depends on workload.

sources.title: SLSA 1.2
sources.supports: Build provenance describes source/build/artifact relationships and level-specific guarantees.
sources.limits: A checksum, self-written JSON record or local signature alone does not establish a SLSA level.

items.title: Complete feedback at the smallest sufficient cost

scope: The selected CI/CD library modules and their authorized project invocations, including source validation, build artifacts, delivery and maintenance.

items.statement:
Deliver surgically precise, fully integrated, synchronized and internally consistent CI/CD.
Code stays modular, structured, hierarchical and clean. Prefer less code through genuine reuse,
not fewer checks disguised as optimization. The library makes a broad set of language, security,
architecture, documentation and deployment capabilities available; each project invokes the full
applicable set for its actual responsibilities. There are no speculative frameworks, duplicate
pipelines or knowingly unfinished work hidden behind green summaries.

The existing LSP, project tests, short PR gates, full main validation and relevant target logs form
the normal feedback loop. Optimize queue time, setup, compilation, cache transfer and redundant
execution while preserving required behavior. The agent acts autonomously, returns to pending CI/CD
and finishes the result.
It does not buy capacity, reopen decisions already settled by the owner or add review machinery
merely to appear thorough. Short PR gates establish merge eligibility; full validation runs on
integrated main before eligible artifact delivery.

items.title: One public modular implementation
items.criteria: Follow a public caller and a private cross-organization caller to the same actual implementation.

condition.text: The subject defines or distributes the reusable library.

items.statement:
The library MUST have one canonical implementation for each shared capability, with distinct CI,
build/artifact and CD responsibilities. Public reusable entrypoints contain no customer topology,
account records or credentials. A project composes only applicable profiles and capabilities;
using a technical module does not migrate its repository or require access to private NDDev tools.
Thin caller-owned jobs and reusable workflows use the same shared actions or native code rather
than independently maintained copies. No new orchestration, review or account-management service
is required by this standard.

items.title: Explicit legal ownership
items.criteria: Compare LICENSE, metadata and the provenance/notices of reused files; no visibility-derived relicensing.

condition.text: The subject publishes or redistributes library material.

items.statement:
The public library MUST retain the selected AGPL-3.0-only terms and accurate notices for incorporated
material. SPDX declarations, package metadata and distributed files agree with the actual grant.
Private source, proprietary corpora and third-party material are not silently relicensed or published.
A repository's visibility alone neither selects a license nor grants redistribution rights.

items.title: Versioned and discoverable module contracts
items.criteria: Check a supported caller, invalid input and compatible upgrade without a duplicated project recipe.

condition.text: The subject supplies or adopts a module interface.

items.statement:
Each delivered module MUST expose its purpose, supported inputs, platform requirements, results and
limits. Project manifests and lockfiles remain the source for project-specific dependencies and
commands. Adopted workflow/action references identify immutable compatible source; updates are normal
reviewed changes, not a mutable main reference silently changing every consumer. Standard edition,
implementation version, runtime schema and consumer product version remain separate identities.

items.title: Visibility and platform select execution
items.criteria: Inspect the full job graph for public/private Linux and Windows/macOS, not only the build job.

condition.text: A job selects an execution provider or runner.

items.statement:
Every library job MUST follow the owner's execution routing, including routing, reporting and other
small helper jobs. Public Linux, Windows and macOS work uses compatible standard free GitHub-hosted runners; public
work never selects Blacksmith or private self-hosted capacity. Private Linux work uses the declared
existing NDDev Linux self-hosted capacity, without hosted or Blacksmith overflow. Private Windows/macOS
work prefers compatible Blacksmith capacity and then compatible standard GitHub capacity only under R-0005. A failed test is not retried on a different provider to obtain a passing result.
The repository that supplies a public workflow does not change the caller's billing or trust context.

items.title: Execution remains within zero additional spend
items.criteria: Verify account-level cost enforcement and concurrent-run handling before any paid-capable dispatch.

condition.text: An invocation can consume provider or storage allowance.

items.statement:
A scheduled run MUST use a demonstrably free allowance or an existing self-hosted resource. Provider
quotas are interpreted in their actual billing units and ownership scope. An alert, card absence or
static estimate alone is not proof of a hard stop on charges. When free admission cannot be
established, the paid-capable route remains disabled; a genuinely free compatible route may be used.
No job buys resources, increases a spending limit or enables a paid add-on. The standards do not
require account churn, duplicate organizations or misrepresentation to obtain allowances.

items.title: Runner selection precedes affected execution
items.criteria: Check unknown-label and cross-organization paths without accidentally scheduling a billed or private job.

condition.text: The implementation schedules a job or chooses execution capacity.

items.statement:
Routing MUST select only configured and available runner capabilities before the relevant job is
scheduled. Unknown platforms, malformed labels and missing capacity remain explicit outcomes, not
silent ubuntu-latest defaults. The caller owns its runner/job when cross-organization reusable
workflow access is insufficient; it may call a public composite implementation. Workflow source
selection and execution context cannot be controlled by untrusted payload fields. A declared runner
name is not evidence of its actual OS, architecture, toolchain or account entitlement.

The routing helper validates configured labels and trust but does not query the native runner
inventory, job access or live queue. Its private self-hosted result reports this limitation
explicitly. Actual availability remains a caller-owned prerequisite established through the
existing runner inventory; label selection alone does not verify R-0006.

items.title: Short PR gates precede full main validation
items.criteria: Trace short PR eligibility, affected full main validation and completed-artifact delivery; duplicate full PR/dev paths and undeclared schedules are absent.

condition.text: The subject defines or invokes source-validation CI.

items.statement:
Pull-request candidates MUST pass a short, finite integration gate before merge. The project owns
its fast syntax, lint/type, relevant unit and critical secret checks; an empty or stale host check
list is not eligibility. Promotion PRs retain the adopted branch and merge policy.
Eligibility evidence binds that workflow path, PR event, repository, current head,
target and relevant base or tested merge context to its latest run attempt. A same-named
main check is not premerge evidence.

Full source validation runs on integrated main pushes. It selects changed components and affected
dependents using the actual validation contract; uncertain scope retains the full set or fails
explicitly. Native builds, SDK/browser matrices, package consumption and target acceptance belong
in this main path when applicable. The same exhaustive suite is not duplicated on every PR or dev
push. Newer main candidates can supersede source-only work without cancelling a target mutation.

GitHub does not build or deploy dev pushes under this baseline. An existing dev server may build
and check dev through its own project-owned path. Absence of that server does not prevent normal
promotion to main. Production readiness still requires successful full main validation.

Declared narrow schedules for advisory refresh, owned registry reclamation or failure feedback
retain an explicit purpose, owner, selected inputs and finite budget. They do not duplicate full
source CI. A manual reproduction is tied to an authorized candidate or failed attempt. Branch and
agent task policy remain owned by their adopted standards; an alternative CI phase model needs
an explicit scoped owner decision.

items.title: Selected coverage includes affected dependents
items.criteria: Exercise shared-input, rename, deleted-file and missing-base changes against real selected components.

condition.text: The subject determines applicable validation coverage.

items.statement:
The run MUST identify its selected profiles and all affected obligations, including dependent
components, shared locks, generated contracts and behavior-changing build configuration. Deletions,
renames and unavailable comparison bases do not produce a false empty change set. An uncertain
impact calculation conservatively retains required coverage or fails explicitly. Selected expensive
checks use finite project-appropriate budgets and relevant PR conditions; required coverage is not
moved to an unobserved future run solely to make a PR fast. Main impact comparison starts from a
completed successful ancestor under the applicable main workflow, not from a failed, cancelled or
still-pending push. Unverified changes remain in scope across superseding pushes.

items.title: Passing means the expected work ran
items.criteria: Inject a missing report, zero-test result and skipped required job; the aggregate cannot pass.

condition.text: The subject summarizes or gates validation results.

items.statement:
An aggregate success MUST account for every expected result for this candidate. No tests discovered,
a missing report, an unsupported selected target, a tool startup failure and an unexpected skipped
job are not passed checks. Non-applicability is distinguishable from inability to execute. Optional
checks are optional because the project contract says so, not because they failed. Success summaries
name what actually ran rather than repeat requested versions or capabilities.

items.title: Results identify their actual inputs
items.criteria: Distinguish changed base, changed library and unchanged deterministic inputs without fabricating a green status.

condition.text: The subject records, compares or reuses validation results.

items.statement:
Reusable results MUST identify the source candidate and significant validation inputs sufficiently
to prevent reuse for a different change. Head/base or tested merge context, workflow implementation,
locks, selected configuration and platform matter where they affect the result. Cache hits and a
matching branch name do not establish check success. Expired vulnerability data and time-dependent
checks retain their own freshness semantics. Identical input results may be reused without ritual
repetition; material changes require the corresponding affected check.

items.title: Toolchains and language profiles are real
items.criteria: Run native positive and failure fixtures for claimed profiles and inspect actual tool/version outputs.

condition.text: A language or SDK profile is selected.

items.statement:
A language or SDK profile MUST execute its selected native build, analysis, test and packaging
operations with compatible resolved toolchains. It verifies the interpreter/compiler that actually
runs and honors project locks without silently rewriting them. Installed tools, caller commands and
platform-specific behavior are handled explicitly. The capability catalog differentiates native
execution, cross-compilation and unverified hardware; declaring a language in YAML is not support.

items.title: Quality gates have stable meanings
items.criteria: Check representative blocking and advisory cases, including scanner failure versus a confirmed finding.

condition.text: The subject applies quality or security gates.

items.statement:
Required build, test, type, secret and selected security/architecture failures MUST affect the run
result. Severity and project thresholds are explicit; the library does not invent one universal
coverage percentage or suppress findings to obtain green. Secondary diagnostics retain a truthful
project-owned disposition. Retries are limited to established transient causes and never erase a
reproducible assertion failure or silently convert flaky behavior into an unconditional pass.

items.title: Architecture checks enforce actual boundaries
items.criteria: A real forbidden dependency fails; a conforming fixture passes; a missing declared module is not green.

condition.text: The project selects an architectural boundary check.

items.statement:
A selected architecture check MUST evaluate declared component responsibilities and dependency
constraints using suitable language-native or established analysis tools. It does not impose a
hexagonal folder skeleton on every script. Empty matched scopes cannot prove a declared boundary;
dynamic/framework entrypoints are considered when evaluating unused code. The result reports the
specific dependency/layer/cycle constraints evaluated, not general architecture perfection.

items.title: Documentation feedback follows executable sources
items.criteria: Check generated drift and broken examples while preserving honest limits for prose review.

condition.text: The subject checks or updates implementation documentation.

items.statement:
Documentation checks MUST use canonical generation, executable examples and meaningful path/link
validation where these apply. Prose is kept aligned by the primary agent in the same engineering
change; an automated link or schema pass does not establish its truth. This library introduces no
mandatory prose digest, periodic attest ritual or automatic reviewer platform. An older adopted
standard's stronger claim rule is changed through an explicit compatible adoption process, not
silently disabled by this workflow. Artifact and provenance digests retain their separate purpose.

items.title: Untrusted checks do not inherit delivery authority
items.criteria: Trace PR code, permissions, artifacts and secrets to each executed command and publication surface.

condition.text: The subject executes repository code or crosses CI/CD trust boundaries.

items.statement:
CI MUST separate untrusted source execution from deployment secrets, write authority and private
host state. Public fork PR code never gains access to the NDDev machine or deployment credentials.
Privileged event handlers do not execute candidate code, artifact scripts or attacker-supplied
commands before validating the actual trust boundary. Private repository visibility alone is not a
proof that every fork or workflow change is trusted. Only required permissions and secrets reach a
job; paid security functionality is not assumed from the fact that its CLI runs on a local machine.

items.title: Failures survive wrappers and shell pipelines
items.criteria: Test setup failure, wrong interpreter, command quoting and a partially prepared replacement.

condition.text: A wrapper or dependent operation executes commands.

items.statement:
An operation MUST preserve relevant process exit status and diagnostic context across wrappers,
pipelines and dependent steps. A failed download/setup cannot become successful installation because
a later shell exited zero. Replacement of a working tool or artifact follows successful preparation
of its replacement. Working directories, environment and tool lookup are consistent across setup,
build and verification; user-controlled text is passed as data where it is not intentionally a
trusted project command.

items.title: Optimization preserves obligations
items.criteria: Compare required outputs and relevant queue/setup/execution costs before and after the optimization.

condition.text: The subject changes execution efficiency or parallelism.

items.statement:
Optimization MUST preserve selected behaviors and trust boundaries. The implementation reduces
queue/setup duplication and the actual critical path, rather than maximize job count. Related small
checks may share a prepared job; independently useful heavy work may be parallelized within actual
CPU, memory and I/O limits. Shards have traceable inputs and aggregate completeness. New runner
features are used only where the deployed runner and tools support them. No benchmark speedup is
claimed from one warm sample or from removed coverage.

items.title: Caches have owners and bounded lifetimes
items.criteria: Check cache compatibility, simultaneous runners and pressure cleanup without losing active/recovery data.

condition.text: The subject reads, writes or reclaims acceleration state.

items.statement:
Caches MUST be acceleration state rather than proof of testing or the sole copy of release data.
Their keys and access boundaries account for relevant dependency, toolchain, platform and trust
inputs. Concurrent writers follow the backend's actual contract. Storage has bounded ownership and
reclamation that preserves active runs, releases and needed recovery artifacts. A broad destructive
cleanup of the shared host or cargo clean before every run is not the default optimization.

items.title: Reports remain useful without storage duplication
items.criteria: Inspect actual exported contents, mode preservation, retention and failure diagnostics.

condition.text: The subject exports or retains run diagnostics or artifacts.

items.statement:
Run diagnostics and artifacts MUST have an identified use, appropriate retention and safe contents.
GitHub logs/summaries serve small feedback; large artifacts are not duplicated merely to create a
report. Permissions, executable bits and hidden inputs needed by an actual package are preserved by
its packaging method. Credentials and private customer data never enter a public artifact, SBOM,
cache or log. A cancelled run's useful diagnostics remain identifiable without retaining its entire
workspace indefinitely.

items.title: CD consumes an eligible integrated result
items.criteria: Reject incomplete, failed and superseded main runs and mismatched artifact attempts or trees; retain explicit historical PR lineage checks.

condition.text: The subject determines eligibility for deployment.

items.statement:
Production deployment MUST consume the exact integrated candidate whose applicable full main CI
completed successfully. The short PR gate establishes merge eligibility, not production readiness.
A trusted completion event or equivalent bounded native wait admits delivery only after that run;
failed, cancelled, incomplete and known-superseded candidates do not start a target mutation.

The artifact is bound to the actual source, configuration, workflow and run attempt. It is not
selected by a mutable latest name or rebuilt after validation. Native admission checks actual
repository, main revision, complete run result and tested tree before consuming the artifact.
The builder may be an existing project-owned server. In that case the applicable full main
workflow validates the exact immutable payload or OCI digests produced by that server and records
them against its successful run and attempt before promotion. Passing source checks for the same
commit alone does not establish that a separately built binary passed artifact validation.
The workflow need not rebuild an already validated artifact or move its builder to GitHub.

Existing callers explicitly adopting the historical PR-artifact contract retain its separately
verified path; the new main baseline is not inferred from an old green PR badge. A merge accepted
by an API remains distinct from deployment and target acceptance.

items.title: Artifact promotion preserves identity
items.criteria: Trace artifact bytes from trusted build through download and target installation.

condition.text: A build artifact is produced, published or promoted.

items.statement:
A supplied release artifact MUST identify its source, build inputs and digest. The same verified
artifact is promoted between compatible environments where possible, with environment configuration
kept separate. Necessary environment-specific rebuilds create a new artifact identity and receive
applicable build validation, not a copied success label. Provenance/attestation claims reflect the
actual build and provider guarantees; a checksum alone neither authenticates an artifact nor grants
SLSA level certification.

items.title: Native deployment is complete rather than declarative only
items.criteria: Run an adapter against an authorized representative target; a generated plan is not an applied result.

condition.text: The project selects a deployment adapter.

items.statement:
A delivered CD module MUST invoke the project's actual configured deployment path and observe its
outcome. First-party adapters remain modular and cover their documented target types without forcing
one universal plan/approval platform. Repository secrets provide required credentials through
supported host features; private GitHub Free is not assumed to have organization secrets or
Environments. Source-only projects and mobile artifacts without store credentials have their real
completion boundary; a fictitious production service is not required.

items.title: The target serializes deployment
items.criteria: Test overlapping attempts to one target, separate targets, and stale attempts after newer delivery.

condition.text: The subject can mutate a shared delivery target.

items.statement:
Concurrent changes to the same delivery target MUST have one effective coordination owner. A unique
attempt/deployment ID is not a target lock. Repository-local concurrency is not a cross-repository
lock. An older attempt cannot overwrite a newer accepted target state, and superseding CI cancellation
is not blindly applied to a running data migration. Read-only or unrelated jobs need not share the
mutation lock. Native target/infrastructure primitives are preferred over a new scheduling service.

items.title: Recovery respects data and partial state
items.criteria: Cover failed health checks, interruption after migration and an incompatible previous artifact.

condition.text: Delivery changes data or encounters partial execution or failure.

items.statement:
Failed or interrupted delivery MUST leave enough truthful state to diagnose and resume or recover
through the existing target mechanism. Data-affecting operations use an appropriate existing backup
or recoverable transition unless the user explicitly waived it for that scope. No-backup authority
is not permission for unrelated deletion. A previous binary is not automatically compatible with
migrated data. Recovery does not silently cancel other agents' work or retry uncertain mutations
before reconciling their actual result.

items.title: Acceptance identifies the running result
items.criteria: Correlate target version, actual scenario, timing and logs, including a deliberately failed scenario.

condition.text: The invocation claims a delivered result.

items.statement:
Successful delivery MUST identify the intended target revision and demonstrate the relevant health
or user scenario with available current diagnostics. A process start or absence of log lines alone
is insufficient when the intended scenario fails. Active DAST, stress and destructive fixtures use
authorized suitable test targets, not live customer data by default. Failure remains visible to the
owning GitHub task; no pipeline auto-closes a delivery parent merely at merge.

items.title: The library is usable outside its publisher account
items.criteria: Use a caller outside the publisher organization and inspect runtime dependency/access requirements.

condition.text: The library exposes public technical entrypoints.

items.statement:
Public technical entrypoints MUST be usable by eligible public and private consumers without reading
proprietary NDDev standards, obtaining a paid plan or copying private manifests. NDDev's own adoption
and catalog rules still apply to its projects. Platform routing is carried by supported consumer
configuration, and public examples contain no real infrastructure identifiers or unprovided secrets.
Build and packaging commands remain runnable through their native project interfaces.

items.title: Claims of support match real verification
items.criteria: Compare each advertised capability against an actual result and its named limits.

condition.text: The implementation declares capabilities or verification coverage.

items.statement:
The implementation MUST distinguish implemented, verified, unsupported and unavailable capabilities.
A profile's success is supported by executed native fixtures and actual caller behavior appropriate
to its claims, not only parsed YAML or a command-recording double. A declared pilot
covers its real adopters; language/CD fixtures cover additional selected modules without fabricated
business deployments. Unexecuted platform or hardware scenarios remain explicitly unverified.

items.title: Adoption and cleanup have a finite scope
items.criteria: Check pilot boundaries, references, retained previous consumers and cleanup of replaced active paths.

condition.text: The task adopts or replaces workflows or related integrations.

items.statement:
Adoption MUST preserve existing consumers and issued identities until an explicit transition replaces
them. Each rollout has an explicit project and infrastructure scope; successful catalog registration or
